title: Eval automation and catalog access flows for curated prompt datasets
creator: Priya Nair
description: Build an automated pipeline and access model for the curated prompt/ground-truth catalog so that any model or config change that can affect output quality triggers targeted evals, owners are notified, and golden datasets remain immutable and auditable. This ticket covers the product definition, acceptance criteria, and stakeholder coordination for catalog access controls, eval trigger policy, and dataset versioning semantics.
background: We currently have ad hoc eval runs and separate golden prompt bundles maintained in different places. Engineering has a golden registry (ENG-7724) but there is no standardized policy that ties model/config changes to the right prompt sets, no fine-grained access model for curated prompts, and no explicit immutable versioning semantics for goldens. This gap causes missed regressions and confusion about who can modify trusted prompt sets used for automatic regression gating.
acceptance_criteria: A1: When a model or inference-config is changed in a rollout, the system evaluates an associated set of prompt bundles automatically within 30 minutes for high-risk changes and within 12 hours for routine changes.
A2: Each golden prompt bundle has an immutable version id (semantic + checksum) and an audit log entry created on publish that records author, approver, reason, and linked eval IDs.
A3: Catalog UI and API expose RBAC roles: Viewer, Editor (propose), Approver (publish/lock), and Emergency-Rollback. Only Approver role can publish a golden bundle to "stable" scope.

A4: Eval results are surfaced in the Console as an alert if any metric regresses beyond configured thresholds, with automated rollback suggestions and a link to the failing examples in the prompt bundle.
A5: PM/Owner can configure trigger sensitivity per-model and per-bundle; default sensitivity uses recommended thresholds from the quality-platform project.
A6: Audit log retention and export path to S3/BigQuery documented and verified in staging.
A7: End-to-end integration test (playback) exists that simulates a model flag flip -> eval trigger -> alert -> approve rollback path.
updates: 2026-02-20: Kickoff meeting with Eng (runtime, infra), Security, and DevEx. Agreed scope and initial acceptance criteria.
2026-02-24: Product/Eng spike approved to prototype a hook in the rollout service for change detection (ENG-8120).
2026-02-27: Design pass completed for catalog publish flow and new Approver role. Microcopy and wireframes uploaded to Confluence.
2026-03-01: Decision to use checksum-based immutable IDs for prompt bundle versions; Eng to implement registry changes (ENG-7724 follow-up).
decisions: D1: Use a two-tier trigger sensitivity (high-risk immediate trigger + routine batched trigger) rather than firing all evals on every change to reduce cost.
D2: Golden bundles are immutable once "stable"; edits create a new version and require Approver sign-off to mark stable.
D3: Default alert thresholds will come from the quality-platform team but are overrideable at the model and bundle level.
D4: Emergency rollback is a separate permission that can be granted temporarily and is auditable (break-glass with 2FA confirmation).
risks: R1: Running many targeted evals on every small config change could materially increase infra costs if not batched or scoped correctly.
R2: Misconfigured RBAC could block urgent fixes; need clear onboarding and an approver rotation policy.
R3: False positives from evals (noise) could cause alert fatigue if thresholds are too tight.
R4: Complexity in mapping model variants to the right prompt bundles; requires a reliable tagging/matching scheme.
next_steps: Finalize API contract for catalog (list/bundle metadata, publish, version, audit) and hand off to Eng by 2026-03-03.
Eng: Implement rollout hooks (ENG-8120) and checksum versioning (ENG-7724 follow-up).
Design: Add microcopy for 'Request Approval' and 'Emergency Rollback' flows, include accessible warnings.
Security: Run a light threat model for the publish/rollback flow and confirm SSO/OAuth constraints.
PM: Draft comms and runbook for customers and internal SREs describing auto-eval behavior and how to opt-out.
blockers: B1: Final RBAC model needs Security sign-off before Approver role is usable in prod.
B2: Need one integration test environment with access to a stable dataset export to validate end-to-end playback.
B3: Small dependencies on the infra quota team for scheduled batched eval capacity; awaiting capacity allocation.
